title: A General Composition Theorem for Approximate Degree
abstract: A longstanding open question in Boolean function complexity asks whether approximate degree composes multiplicatively under block composition. Although a general multiplicative upper bound is known, matching lower bounds have previously been established only for restricted classes of functions. We resolve this question for all total Boolean functions by proving the matching lower bound. Together with Sherstov's upper bound, our result shows that, for every pair of total Boolean functions $f:\{0,1\}^n\to\{0,1\}$ and $g:\{0,1\}^m\to\{0,1\}$, \[ \widetilde{deg}(f\circ g) = Θ\!\left( \widetilde{deg}(f)\,\widetilde{deg}(g) \right), \] where $\widetilde{deg}$ denotes constant-error approximate degree.
summary: This paper resolves a major open problem in Boolean function complexity by proving that the approximate degree of block-composed functions composes multiplicatively. The authors establish the tight bound $\widetilde{deg}(f\circ g) = \Theta(\widetilde{deg}(f)\,\widetilde{deg}(g))$ using sophisticated tools from harmonic analysis and polynomial approximation theory.
main_problem: The paper addresses the open question of whether the approximate degree of block-composed Boolean functions composes multiplicatively.
main_result: It proves that for arbitrary total Boolean functions $f$ and $g$, the approximate degree satisfies $\widetilde{deg}(f\circ g) = \Theta(\widetilde{deg}(f)\,\widetilde{deg}(g))$.
method: The proof involves establishing a matching lower bound by using advanced techniques involving trigonometric polynomials, squarefree extraction, and constructing specific probability measures derived from dual witnesses.
